standard_prerequisites.name: The Bockstein operators beta attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules and a nonzerodivisor vanish exactly where the reduction modulo f^2 surjects onto the reduction modulo f, and their vanishing implies the condition defining the locus E
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 28231-28233 and again at proof lines 28250-28252
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the two descriptions of E and supplies part (4).

standard_prerequisites.name: The shifted complex has finite locally free terms of the given ranks when the Fitting ideals are principal
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the terms of the shifted complex finite locally free, which is what allows the local splitting in the proof of part (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: An ideal defined by a universal property of a map between free modules contains exactly the elements by which the map can be made to split as prescribed, so the local vanishing of that ideal is read off from the existence of a compatible direct sum decomposition
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the vanishing of the localized ideals J_i from the displayed splitting, which is the whole content of part (3).

core_obligations: Identify the two descriptions of the locus E using the vanishing beta lemma, and record that the final statement of that lemma gives part (4) (proof lines 28231-28233).

Prove part (1) and part (2): the ideals J_i are finitely generated and vanish for almost all i because the complex is bounded, so their sum J is finitely generated, and the surjection onto the quotient by J is then of finite presentation by definition (proof lines 28235-28238).

Prove part (3): use the lemma on local freeness of the shifted complex to get finite locally free terms of ranks r_i, consider the displayed map (1, d^i) between the reductions, and for a prime in E write the localization of the reduction of the shifted term as a direct sum compatible with that map; the universal property of J_i then forces J_i localized to vanish (proof lines 28240-28259).

Prove part (5): display the commuting square expressing the differential of the shifted complex, tensor it with C and use the two Xy-pic diagrams to see that the terms become direct sums of direct summands of the corresponding terms on the right, compatible with the differential (proof lines 28264-28301).

Conclude that the differential identifies the second direct summand in degree i with a direct summand of the first direct summand in degree i+1, so the cohomology in degree i is a quotient of two finite projective summands and is therefore finite projective, which is the assertion of part (5) (proof lines 28302-28305).
proof_roadmap: Match the two descriptions of E and import part (4) from the vanishing beta lemma (proof lines 28231-28233).
Get finiteness of J from the finite generation of its finitely many nonzero summands and reformulate the quotient as being of finite presentation (proof lines 28235-28238).

For part (3), localize at a prime of E, write the reduction of the shifted term as a compatible direct sum using local freeness, and read off the vanishing of the localized J_i (proof lines 28240-28259).
For part (5), draw the two diagrams, decompose the terms after tensoring with C and identify the cohomology with a quotient of finite projective summands (proof lines 28264-28305).
difficulty_reason: The statement collects five facts about the ideal J of the Bockstein operators attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules over a nonzerodivisor, among them its finite generation, the finite presentation of the quotient C, the vanishing of J along a locus described in two equivalent ways, and the local freeness of the cohomology of the shifted complex after tensoring with C (statement lines 28197-28228). The proof identifies the two descriptions of the locus, then proves the finiteness from boundedness of the complex, then obtains the vanishing of J on the locus by localizing and using that the shifted terms are finite locally free, so that the localized reduction splits in a way compatible with the map (1, d^i) and the universal property of J_i applies (proof lines 28230-28259). The final part is proved by exhibiting two diagrams whose horizontal arrows are compatible with direct sum decompositions, which identifies the differential as an injection of a summand and makes the cohomology a quotient of finite projective modules (proof lines 28264-28305). The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of the same section, all carried as navigation stubs.
